A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Analytic-Precond research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, FID measurements, training curves and a Gaussian-mixture trajectory study in Section 4, with generated samples in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the generated samples in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same generalized ODE, analytic coefficient optimization and backward-Euler preconditioning. The model architecture, losses and sampling procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain CIFAR-10 conditional/unconditional, FFHQ unconditional, ImageNet conditional and the same one-dimensional Gaussian-mixture example. Table 2's ImageNet resolution inconsistency with the experimental description also persists in both versions.

E2.justification: The CM/CTM comparisons, CTM with BCM preconditioning in Figure 5, and GAN-loss comparisons in Figure 6 retain identical comparator membership. The newly cited attention methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Table 3 and v1 Appendix C.1–C.3, now v3 Appendix B.1–B.3, retain the same training budgets, batch sizes, coefficient-estimation sample counts, Heun solver, timestep schedules and FID evaluation on 50,000 generated samples.

E4.justification: The coefficient analyses, GAN-loss compatibility study, Gaussian-mixture trajectory analysis and appendix sample comparisons are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same evaluation-seed statement and coefficient-estimation procedure. Neither adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2's numerical entries and the plotted results and sample images are unchanged. For example, unconditional CIFAR-10 at NFE=2 remains 3.83 FID for CTM and 3.77 for CTM + Ours in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, derivations and Proposition 3.1's assumptions and consistency-gap bound are unchanged. Its proof, including Equations 18–26, moves from Appendix B.1 to Appendix A.1 without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and main conclusion retain the same contributions: theoretically motivated analytic preconditioning, improved trajectory alignment and 2×–3× training acceleration for multi-step CTMs. The scope of these central claims is unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit qualification that final FID improvements are relatively small. Its new limitations paragraph also consolidates the previously discussed long-jump/single-step limitation and adds misuse and social-bias caveats; existing mechanism explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.4 and Table 4 provide resource URLs and license information for the datasets and EDM/CM/CTM implementations. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, computation costs and training details are retained.

R1.justification: Related work gains one sentence on quantized or sparse attention, citing SageAttention, SageAttention2 and SpargeAttn. The remaining discussion is moved from Appendix A to Section 4. The additional CIFAR-10 bibliography entry duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: Related work moves into the main text, with corresponding section and appendix renumbering. Limitations, acknowledgments and a license subsection are added, while most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the resource-license Table 4 and adjusts figure/table placement and surrounding layout, including Figures 4, 5 and 7 and Table 3. Existing scientific figures, captions and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 more explicitly acknowledges the limited final FID gains and supplies useful resource-access and licensing information in Section 6 and Appendix B.4. These additions modestly improve transparency and documentation; the method, proofs and empirical validation remain unchanged.
